payload.claim: The only ordering test declares gates as {"tests": tests, "lint": lint}, so `tests` is always the first key and lands at results[0] before insertion. Changing `position = next(i for i, r in enumerate(results) if r.gate == "tests") + 1` in saffron/gates/runner.py (line 264) to the hard-coded `position = 1` keeps this test green — witness still lands at index 1 — while breaking the case the test's own docstring claims to cover ('regardless of where `tests` sits in the repo's declared gate order'): with gates declared as {"lint": lint, "tests": tests}, the hard-coded version would insert `witness` before `tests` instead of after it. No test in the diff declares `tests` anywhere but first, so the dynamic-position claim central to the first acceptance criterion is unverified for that case.
